rubric_name: Operational rubric aligned with Lab 03 official grading sheet

score_model.notes: Each criterion receives a score from 0 to 10. The final score is the weighted sum of all criteria on a 0-10 scale.

notes: Operational rubric derived from the official sheet, grading guidelines, and FilmNow instructions.

criteria.name: Basic Functionality
criteria.description: Evaluates the operation of the main lab features, such as registering movies, listing movies, detailing movies, and manipulating the HotList. Localized errors should generate proportional deductions; only use very low scores when the main functionality is absent or clearly incorrect. Purely cosmetic differences in messages, such as accents, casing, or exclamation marks, should not generate deductions on their own if the meaning remains the same.

criteria.name: Unit Tests
criteria.description: Evaluates JUnit tests for Movie and FilmNow classes. Differentiate between total absence of tests, present but incomplete tests, and extensive tests. Do not automatically zero the score if there is real evidence of tests, even if coverage is partial.

criteria.name: Class Design
criteria.description: Evaluates whether the main lab classes were created and modeled appropriately for the problem. For first-year students, value evidence that the student understands the central idea of modeling Movie and FilmNow as separate classes, even with localized imperfections.

criteria.name: Object References and Composition
criteria.description: Evaluates composition, object creation, and proper use of references between classes. Focus on the understanding of how one class uses objects of another, without over-penalizing small implementation slips if the main idea is correct.

criteria.name: Collections and Arrays
criteria.description: Evaluates the structures used to store movies and the HotList, respecting lab constraints. If the main structure serves the problem, minor implementation details should not excessively lower the score.

criteria.name: Separation of Concerns
criteria.description: Evaluates whether responsibilities are minimally well-separated between the UI, domain classes, and the manager. For first-year students, concentrate deductions on excessive concentration of rules in a single place, but recognize when some correct separation exists.

criteria.name: Readability and Documentation
criteria.description: Evaluates naming, organization, comments, and public Javadoc. Do not confuse lack of polish with total lack of learning: use light to moderate deductions when the code is understandable, even without excellent documentation.
